title: Region-aware token SLI smoothing, staged circuit-breaker thresholds, and dashboard rollout
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's current token-level latency SLIs are noisy in low-volume regions and oscillate during transient spikes. This makes both automated circuit-breaker triggers and on-call dashboards difficult to interpret during regional failovers. We need a combined approach: smoother SLIs for reliable alerting + staged circuit-breaker thresholds that tie into multi-region failover policies and graceful load-shedding rules.

Goals:
1) Define and implement token-level SLI smoothing (exponential + dynamic window) per region/model/route to reduce false positives while preserving signal for real regressions.
2) Introduce staged circuit-breaker thresholds (warning/soft-trip/hard-trip) derived from smoothed SLIs and regional capacity.
3) Build a focused dashboard set for operators showing smoothed vs raw token latency percentiles, regional traffic heatmaps, CB state timelines, and load-shedding actions.
4) Create a rollout plan: canary in 1 region, evaluate for 2 weeks, then global ramp with auto-fallback.

Instrumentation design notes:
- Golden signals to instrument: latency (token P50/P90/P95/P99), error rate (by failure class), saturation (GPU/queue depth), and request queue time.
- Token SLI computation: compute per-shard token latency histogram at ingestion (within runtime). Apply a two-stage smoothing: (a) short-window EWMA (alpha=0.33, window approx 30s) to remove micro-noise, (b) long-window percentile stabilizer (rolling 5m) to avoid reaction to single transient spikes. Store both smoothed and raw values.
- Low-volume regions: fall back to aggregated cross-region baseline when sample count < 100 tokens/min for a given model/route.
- Threshold derivation: baselines come from percentile baselines computed over last 28 days per region/model. Warning threshold = baseline * 1.5 + 50ms, soft-trip = baseline * 2.5 + 150ms, hard-trip = baseline * 4 + 400ms. Values can be overridden per-customer SLA.
- Circuit-breaker integration: CB state machine will evaluate smoothed P95 and smoothed tail (P99) with independent counters. Soft-trip moves traffic to degraded tier (token truncation / lower batch sizes / quantized model), hard-trip triggers failover to alternate region/model variant according to routing policy.
- Load-shedding actions: define graded shedding steps tied to CB states: 1) non-critical background requests deprioritized; 2) opt-in user requests sampled; 3) enforced rate limits per API key with graceful 429 responses that include retry info.

Dashboard & Alerts:
- New dashboards (Grafana):
  * "Smoothed vs Raw Token Latency" (by region/model/route) with toggle to overlay raw 95/99.
  * "CB State Timeline" (region x time heatmap) showing transitions and active load-shedding rules.
  * "Regional Traffic and Saturation" with GPU utilization, queue depth, and sample count.
  * "Low-volume fallback telemetry" panel to show when cross-region baseline was used.
- Alerting:
  * P0 Alert: hard-trip for >1 minute in a customer-facing region -> page on-call.
  * P1 Alert: soft-trip triggered in multiple regions within 10 minutes -> warn SRE rotation.
  * P2 Alert: sustained smoothed P95 > warning threshold for 15m -> slack incident channel.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement smoothing and dashboard panels in staging.
2) Canary deploy to eu-west-1 (single tenant traffic) for 14 days. Monitor false positive rate and SLO regression.
3) If canary stable, enable for all non-critical routes for 48h.
4) Full region enable with release flag. Auto-fallback disabled for first 24h.

Links / artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231
- Grafana draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/4X7sK/smoothed-token-latency
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Region-aware+SLI+Smoothing+Proposal
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/region-cb-load-shed

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Need a small runtime tag to emit per-token micro-buckets; requires a patch to ingestion path that adds ~1% CPU for the runtime leader.
- Storage: smoothed metrics retained for 30d at 1m granularity, raw buckets at 1m for 7d. Evaluate cost impact with Metrics team.
- Edge case: model warmup events produce high latency; exclude warmup windows using model-load markers.

Success metrics:
- Reduce on-call false-positive CB trips by >=60% in canary region during test window.
- Maintain or decrease customer-facing P50 latency after enabling smoothing + load-shedding for degraded traffic.
- Dashboards show clear handoffs: ability to trace CB trigger -> load-shed action -> routing failover within 2 clicks.
acceptance_criteria: Smoothed and raw token latency panels exist in Grafana and match staged metrics in staging
Circuit-breaker evaluates smoothed P95/P99 and can transition through warning/soft/hard states in test harness
Canary deploy completed with false-positive trips reduced >=60% vs baseline
Runbook updated with steps for CB manual override and rollback
Monitoring alerts configured and tested end-to-end (pager and slack)
